newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly lower after late selloff.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly lower after late selloff.

text.p: CME lumber futures posted both sharp rallies and substantial breaks before ending mostly lower, traders said.
Late selling by Cargill Investor Services in January and pressure from locals in March late weighed on futures after two early rallies, they said.

Early buying by Prudential Securities hit buy stops but the market ran into mixed resistance and prices retreated at midsession. The market rallied again around midday on fresh demand from Prudential but eased late as buying lacked follow-through, they said.
Lumber closed off $2.30 per tbf to up $2.40 with January up $1.40 at $378.70 and March off $0.90 at $370.30 per tbf.

However, futures appear to be showing a firmer undertone as spreads have turned. Bull spreading dominated the market again Tuesday and this is in contrast to the active bear spreading the market saw on the recent sharp decline following tumbling cash markets, they added.
"Spreads were turning from bear to bull and indicate bottoming in the (futures) market," one trader said.
Cash sources also noted that the cash market appeared to be nearing a bottom after tumbling $100 per tbf recently.

Some interest was starting to develop in cash at the lower price levels, especially as the cash market usually starts to show seasonal support from reduced production during the holiday periods. However, current cash trade remained slow as both mills and dealers were getting ready to take extended days off for the Thanksgiving Day holiday, they added.
